Someone Paid New Ford Mustang Dark Horse Money for an Old 2017 Shelby GT350R
13 photos
Photo: Cars&Bids
The Shelby GT350 and the Shelby GT350R versions of the S550-generation Ford Mustang will finally get proper successors in the modern era, as the Blue Oval is preparing the Cobra and Cobra R as we speak.
However, if the older models still tickle your fancy, then you should know that you can still buy a barely-driven example if you know where to look and are patient enough. A brand-new one tends to hit the market every now and then, too. As for the one pictured above, it had under 3,800 miles (~6,100 km) on the clock at the time of cataloging.
Finished in Oxford White on top of an ebony interior, this 2017 Ford Mustang Shelby GT350R features 19-inch carbon fiber wheels, MagneRide damping, Brembo brakes, and the R Electronics Package. It also has a carbon fiber rear wing, Recaro sports seats for the driver and front passenger, and cloth and suede upholstery with red contrast stitching.
Powering it is a flat-plane crank Voodoo V8. The 5.2-liter engine develops 526 hp (392 kW/534 ps) and 429 lb-ft (582 Nm) of torque. Everything is channeled to the rear wheels through a six-speed manual transmission. This model completed the standing quarter mile in 12 seconds, and took less than four seconds to zip from 0 to 60 mph (0 to 97 kph).
Photo: Cars&Bids The listing mentions some scratches on certain exterior panels on the known flaws category. Moreover, this Ford Mustang Shelby GT350R also has a split in the paint protection film on the left front fender, according to the seller. The muscle car was offered with a clean Carfax report revealing that it has been registered in the state of Florida since new.
This ride was serviced in February 2026, when it had its four tires replaced, mounted, and balanced, and an alignment performed. It also had its engine oil and filter changed then, at 3,401 miles (5,473 km). In March 2025, the engine oil and filter were changed, the clutch system was bled, and the brake fluid was flushed/changed, at 2,890 miles (4,651 km). The engine oil and filter were also changed in April 2024 and July 2023, at 2,215 miles (3,565 km) and 747 miles (1,202 km), respectively.
Other items included in the sale were the Ford flat-plane crankshaft owner’s kit, the owner’s manuals, two keys, and the window sticker that reveals that this muscle car originally changed hands for $66,395. The Ford Mustang Shelby GT350R recently found a new home on Cars&Bids, where the seller , who reportedly bought it in January 2026, adding some 300 miles (500 km) since, let it go in return for $72,000.
That’s actually more than the original retail price, and it is pretty much new S650 Ford Mustang Dark Horse territory, as the latter starts at $65,080 (MSRP) or $70,075 when it comes to the Dark Horse Premium trim.
